source.title: Dissecting components of reward: 'liking', 'wanting', and learning

confidence_rationale: Canonical evidence that hedonic 'liking' is a separately-instantiated channel doubly dissociable from motivational 'wanting'/dopaminergic vigour. But predominantly rodent pharmacology/lesion synthesis establishing NEUROCHEMICAL dissociation, silent on separate learnability and on improves-conversion; substantial abstraction to map a hedonic hotspot onto a gating-layer channel.
failure_signatures: 'Liking' is shown to be hard to move (dopamine and most manipulations fail to enhance it; it lives in small fragile opioid/GABA hotspots) -- so a liking channel may be low-variance / weakly action-coupled, exactly the profile a gating learner would down-weight to zero, reproducing rather than relieving a conversion ceiling.
The components normally co-occur and interact; clean separability is a laboratory dissociation, not the default operating regime.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Reward decomposes into three dissociable components -- 'liking' (hedonic impact), 'wanting' (incentive salience), and learning -- with partly separable substrates; dopamine drives wanting but not liking, and liking is generated by restricted opioid/GABA hotspots separate from the dopaminergic incentive system.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports including 'hedonic liking' as a finer channel distinct from the dopaminergic/vigour channel rather than collapsing both into one value signal.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Establishes neurochemical/anatomical dissociation of liking vs wanting; silent on whether a learner can SEPARATELY learn them, and silent on whether finer granularity improves action conversion. Mostly rodent pharmacology/lesion.
mapping.source_context: Synthesis review of rodent (and some human) reward-component dissociation studies.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical for the channel-distinctness premise; the low-malleability of liking is itself a concrete predicted failure mode for the falsifier.
